name: The Mekong Delta
tagline: A flat green maze of rivers, canals, orchards and floating markets, where life moves by boat and the best breakfast is a noodle soup served from a sampan.
highlight: A dawn boat to a floating market, with fruit boats piled high and vendors hanging their wares from tall poles.
shortDescription: Vietnam's rice bowl: a delta of waterways south of Ho Chi Minh City with floating markets at Can Tho, fruit orchards, homestays, coconut candy workshops and a slow river pace.
metaDescription: A Mekong Delta travel guide: Can Tho and the Cai Rang floating market, Ben Tre, My Tho, Vinh Long homestays, Chau Doc, food, when to go, how to get there from Ho Chi Minh City and a three-day plan.
nearestAirport: Can Tho (VCA), or Tan Son Nhat, Ho Chi Minh City (SGN), about 2–3.5 hours away
knownFor: Floating markets, rivers, orchards, homestays, coconut products
goodFor: River life, food, cycling, homestays, a slow pace

image.file: File:Can Tho, Vietnam, Floating market, Early morning.jpg
image.alt: Boats gathering at the Cai Rang floating market near Can Tho in the early morning

intro: The Mekong River ends its journey of 4,900 km in southern Vietnam, splitting into a fan of channels that empty into the South China Sea. The delta they form is one of the most fertile places in Asia, producing much of Vietnam's rice, fish and tropical fruit. It is a flat landscape of paddies, orchards, fish farms and villages linked by waterways, where boats are still as important as roads.

For visitors, the delta offers a glimpse of everyday rural life in the south, at a slow pace. Typical trips include boat rides through narrow canals lined with nipa palms, visits to workshops making coconut candy, rice paper and puffed rice, orchard walks with fruit tasting, and overnight stays in homestays. The most famous sight is the floating market at Cai Rang near Can Tho, where traders sell produce from boats, though it has shrunk as roads and bridges have improved.

The delta is easy to visit on a day trip from Ho Chi Minh City, but it repays a night or two, particularly for the early-morning atmosphere. Many visitors also use it as a route to or from Cambodia, by boat from Chau Doc to Phnom Penh.

whyVisit.intro: The Mekong Delta is a peaceful contrast to Vietnam's cities, and shows a different side of the country.

points.title: Waterways and boats
points.text: Life on and beside the rivers, from small sampans to big barges.

points.title: Orchards and workshops

points.title: Easy from Saigon

attractionsIntro: The delta is large, and most visitors choose one or two bases.

attractions.name: The Cai Rang floating market, Can Tho
attractions.text: The largest floating market in the delta, where wholesalers sell fruit and vegetables from big boats, hanging samples from poles. Best at dawn, from about 5 to 8 am.
attractions.tip: Book a boat the evening before, and go early.

attractions.name: Can Tho

image.file: File:Can Tho, Vietnam, Floating Market, Boats.jpg
image.alt: Boats loaded with fruit and vegetables at a floating market near Can Tho

attractions.text: The largest city in the delta, with a pleasant waterfront, markets and pagodas, and a base for boat trips.

attractions.name: My Tho and Ben Tre

image.alt: A wide channel of the Mekong River in the delta

attractions.text: Delta towns about 1.5 to 2 hours from Ho Chi Minh City, known for canals, coconut candy workshops and orchard visits. Ben Tre is the coconut capital of Vietnam.
attractions.tip: A good day trip for those short of time.

attractions.name: Vinh Long and homestays
attractions.text: A delta town with islands, orchards and family-run homestays, quieter than My Tho.
attractions.tip: Book a homestay for the evening.

attractions.name: Chau Doc
attractions.text: A town near the Cambodian border with a floating village, Sam Mountain, Tra Su Cajuput forest and a mixed culture of Vietnamese, Khmer, Cham and Chinese people.
attractions.tip: Take the boat to Phnom Penh if heading to Cambodia.

thingsToDoIntro: Most activities revolve around the rivers and orchards.

thingsToDo.title: Visit a floating market at dawn
thingsToDo.text: Take a boat to the Cai Rang market and have breakfast on the water.

thingsToDo.title: Take a canoe through the canals
thingsToDo.text: A rowing boat takes you through narrow channels under nipa palms.

thingsToDo.title: Try a homestay
thingsToDo.text: Sleep in a village house and eat home-cooked meals.

thingsToDo.title: Watch a coconut candy workshop
thingsToDo.text: See coconut milk boiled and cut into sweets.

thingsToDo.title: Cycle through orchards
thingsToDo.text: Quiet paths pass fruit trees, and you can taste tropical fruit.

thingsToDo.title: Take a boat to Cambodia
thingsToDo.text: A river route from Chau Doc to Phnom Penh, about 5 to 6 hours.

foodIntro: The delta's food is fresh, sweet and based on river fish, rice and tropical fruit.

foods.name: Elephant-ear fish
foods.text: A deep-fried whole fish served upright, wrapped in rice paper with herbs.
foods.whereToTry: Restaurants in My Tho and Can Tho.

foods.name: Hu tieu My Tho
foods.text: A clear noodle soup with pork and seafood, the local breakfast.

foods.name: Coconut candy
foods.text: Chewy sweets made from coconut cream, from Ben Tre.

foods.name: Banh xeo
foods.text: Sizzling pancakes with pork and shrimp.

foods.name: Tropical fruit
foods.text: Mango, dragon fruit, rambutan and durian, according to season.

accommodation.intro: Choose between a hotel in Can Tho and a homestay on the river.

areas.name: Can Tho
areas.text: Hotels along the waterfront and in the centre.

gettingThere.intro: The delta lies south and west of Ho Chi Minh City.

options.mode: Tour from Ho Chi Minh City
options.text: Day tours to My Tho or Ben Tre, or two-day trips to Can Tho, are widely available.
About 3 to 4 hours from Ho Chi Minh City to Can Tho, and 1.5 to 2 hours to My Tho.
options.detail: The new expressways have cut journey times.

options.text: Flights from Hanoi and some other cities.

gettingAround.intro: Boats, bicycles and taxis cover the delta.

options.text: The main way to see the rivers and markets.
Useful in Can Tho and towns.

bestTime.headline: December–April
bestTime.summary: The delta is hot and humid all year, with a dry season and a wet season, and the water level rises from August to November.

seasons.text: Sunny and comfortable, though hot by April.
Afternoon showers, green fields and fruit season.
Heavy rain, with the rivers in flood.
Many businesses close, though the celebrations are vivid.

bestTime.avoid: Tet, when many boats and shops are closed.

itinerary.title: Two days in the Mekong Delta
itinerary.intro: A night in Can Tho, with the floating market at dawn.

days.title: To Can Tho
days.morning: Leave Ho Chi Minh City for My Tho or Ben Tre.
days.afternoon: A canal boat and an orchard visit.

days.title: The floating market
days.afternoon: Return to Ho Chi Minh City.

tipsIntro: A few tips help you enjoy the delta.
tips: Stay a night, to see the floating market at dawn.
Choose a small boat, not a big group boat.
Bring insect repellent and sun protection.
Bargain for boats, and agree the price beforehand.
Do not expect the floating markets to be as big as in old photos.

faq.q: How many days do you need in the Mekong Delta?
faq.a: One day for a taste, two days with a night in Can Tho for the floating market.

faq.q: Is the floating market worth it?
faq.a: Yes, at dawn. It is smaller than in the past, but still atmospheric.

faq.q: What is the best time to visit?
faq.a: December to April, the dry season.

faq.q: Can I do it as a day trip from Ho Chi Minh City?
faq.a: Yes, to My Tho or Ben Tre. Can Tho is better with a night.
Yes, generally. Use reputable boat operators.

faq.q: Can I travel to Cambodia by boat?
faq.a: Yes, from Chau Doc to Phnom Penh, about 5 to 6 hours. Check the visa requirements.
